Small purchases under fifty pounds may be made by any committee member on their own authority
and claimed back with a receipt; between fifty and two hundred pounds the treasurer's agreement
is needed in advance; above two hundred the committee's. The limits are in the constitution and
change only at a general meeting.

Equipment other than boats -- oars, riggers, the launch, the trailer, the rowing machines -- is listed
in the asset register with its date of purchase, its cost and where it lives, and the register is checked
against the boathouse once a year on the first winter work day. An item that cannot be found is
written up at the next meeting, and an item that was never on the register in the first place is added
with an estimate and a note. The register is what the insurer asks for after a break-in, and the one
year it was out of date the claim took four months.

The treasurer's handover happens at the annual general meeting and is a meeting of its own, with
the outgoing and incoming treasurers, the chair and the examiner, the deed box opened and its
contents listed, the bank mandate changed on the day, and these notes read through together. It
takes an afternoon and has never been regretted.

Questions from members about the money are answered by the treasurer, in person where
possible, and are welcome even when they are awkward, because a member who asks is a member
who has read the accounts. A question the treasurer cannot answer on the spot is answered in
writing within the week, and a question that turns out to have found a mistake is thanked for in the
next report by name if the member agrees. The club has had three treasurers who took questions
badly and none of them lasted, which is the lesson.

The budget for the year is set by the committee in February from the treasurer's draft, which starts
from last year's actuals and changes only what there is a reason to change. It is one page. Each line

provenance.key:
memory stick that lives in the deed box, and the previous year's sheet is locked as soon as the
accounts are approved and is never edited again.

The year end is the thirty-first of March. The treasurer closes the books in the first week of April,
the independent examiner sees them by the end of April, and the examined accounts go to the
members with the notice of the annual general meeting. An examiner who finds something is
thanked and the something is fixed before the accounts go out, not explained at the meeting.

The examiner's fee is £1,250.00 a year and is the one professional cost the club does not shop
around for, because an examiner who knows the club finds the things a new one would not. The fee
is agreed in writing in January and paid in May on receipt of the report, and the letter of
engagement is reviewed by the committee every three years so that the arrangement is a decision
and not a habit.

The reserve policy is written down and short: three months of running costs in the current account,
the repairs reserve and the boat fund in the deposit account, and anything above that spent on the
members within two years. Money held for no reason is money the members could have had in
lower subscriptions, and the committee has to say each year why it is holding what it holds, in a
sentence a new member could follow.

Gift Aid is claimed every year on the subscriptions of members who have signed the declaration,
which is most of them, and the claim is worth roughly a tenth of the subscription income. The
declarations are kept with the membership records and the claim is prepared by the treasurer from
the membership secretary's list, checked by the examiner, and submitted in May, with a copy of the
list kept in the deed box for the examiner.

Debts to the club are chased by letter, then by a conversation, then by the committee, and are
written off by a committee vote if they are not paid within a year, with the member's name minuted.
It has been needed four times in twenty years, and each time the member had already left the club,
which is a comfort of a kind and not much of one, and the letters are kept in the box with the rest.
